note: V16 (Amenti.live, the Treasure fleet at night off Ireland), 27 Nov 2026: the paintings for the 360-degree sky, in Van Gogh's night manner. Claude joins the chosen takes round the compass, as Whitby's were. Same horizon height in every beat so they join.
style: An oil painting in the manner of Vincent van Gogh's The Starry Night (1889) and Starry Night Over the Rhone (1888): thick impasto, bold rhythmic directional brushstrokes everywhere, a night sky of swirling wind currents and coiling eddies in ultramarine, cobalt and Prussian blue, large stars blazing chrome yellow and white with radiant halos of concentric rings, warm lamplight in orange and gold. A wide panorama seen from a boat low on the water at night. The horizon and shoreline are perfectly level and sit low, one fifth of the way up the picture, with the lower fifth dark blue water painted in short horizontal strokes. The left and right edges continue naturally into more sky and water, with no vignette, so the pictures can be joined side by side. No ships, no boats, no people, no text, no signature, no frame, no border, no black bars.

beats.text: Cobh in Cork Harbour, Ireland, at night, seen across the water. Rows of tall narrow terraced houses painted in bright colours, blue, yellow, pink, green, step up a steep hillside, their windows glowing gold. Near the top of the hill, a little right of centre, St Colman's Cathedral, a great Gothic Revival church with one tall pointed spire, rises dark against the swirling sky. Along the quay at the water's edge a line of gas lamps throws long broken streaks of gold light down across the black water. A crescent moon blazes orange-yellow in the upper left.

The open Atlantic off the south coast of Ireland at night, the companion to a painting of the town of Cobh. Dark water to a level horizon under an enormous swirling Van Gogh sky of coiling wind currents and many blazing stars with ringed halos. Near the right edge, low dark headlands and, small on the point, a white lighthouse with a warm lamp (Roche's Point). Otherwise only sky and sea.

The low dark hills and islands of Cork Harbour, Ireland, at night: a long gentle shoreline of dark green-black hills along a level horizon, a few scattered cottage windows glowing gold, a squat old stone fort on a low island in the middle distance (Spike Island). Above, a vast swirling Van Gogh sky of coiling wind currents and blazing stars with concentric halos.
